task_context.problem_statement: Given a square matrix of size N*N given as a list of lists, where each cell is associated with a specific cost. A path is defined as a specific sequence of cells that starts from the top-left cell move only right or down and ends on bottom right cell. We want to find a path with the maximum average over all existing paths. Average is computed as total cost divided by the number of cells visited in the path.

For any cell (i, j), you can only arrive from the cell above it or the cell to its left. How would you express the value of the current cell based on those two possible previous cells?

You've got the general transition correct. For the first row, there is no cell 'above', so you can only come from the left. Similarly, for the first column, you can only come from above. Try sketching out how you would initialize these edges using a simple cumulative sum of the costs along those boundaries.

Okay, so I'd loop through the first row and add each cost to the previous total, then do the same for the first column. Then I fill the rest of the matrix using the max transition. Finally, I divide the value at the bottom-right cell by (2N-1) to get the average. Is that the right way to do it?

You have correctly identified the initialization of the boundaries, the transition logic for the interior of the matrix, and the final step to convert the maximum sum into the maximum average. You now have a complete logical roadmap to implement the function in Python.
